title: Dragon's Lair
build: Software Projects disk, alternate D64 with LA–LJ files

records.c: The first copied byte in the scene record is $04. The caller starts executing one byte later.
Save and reload the caller stack pointer, hide sprites and install raster target $2899. Draw the initial ramp sections one at a time before copying sprite shapes out of $5B00.
Restore the saved stack and digit glyphs, configure the character screen and raster handler, and reset the section index and movement state before drawing the ramps.
Call $238B for each section number from 1 through 9, with six timer waits between sections. Disable sprites during the build.
Copy a 256-byte page from $5B00 to $5C00 before writing the padding bytes in the destination sprite records.
Sample the joystick and wait twice. Update the scene, branch to $1FCE when $2937 is set, then test fire in bit 4 of $28. The fire path passes neutral input onward after resetting $28 to $FF.
Set the active animation flag and clear its frame counter, install the initial poses, then run the fire animation update.
Update the four sprite frames and advance the section transition before returning to the joystick loop.
Decrement the sampling countdown. When it expires, reload it with 2 and latch sprite and background collisions before updating sprites 7 through 5.
Use the active slot to check two bit masks and step its four-frame counter when its mask is set. Select the subsequent sprite records and combine them with the slot selection.

Advance the transition counter and redraw the preceding section at count 11. Through count 12, move the four Dirk sprites vertically by the indexed displacement and horizontally according to the facing state.
Select a six- or seven-step animation from the saved facing state. Update sprite 0 and sprite 4, with offsets from the selected frame table. On completion hide sprite 4 and restore the normal poses.
With X as the frame index, set the mirrored orientation and install the companion and first sprite pointers. Pass the indexed offsets to the sprite 4 position routine.

Choose and orient four frames from the saved direction, rearrange their sprite slots for the fire pose and enable sprite 4. If the orientation has changed, negate the X offsets in both companion tables.
Add the signed offsets at $29FC/$29FD to sprite 0 to position sprite 4. Carry and borrow adjust its high X bit.

Save the requested section number in $2962. Use it to select an input pointer, a screen address and a stopping address from the ramp tables. Compute the companion colour address by adding $98 to the screen high byte.
Add $50 to the source, two rows of forty cells, and put that address in the screen destination pointer. Add $9800 for the colour destination and fall through to the row copier.

Copy each row's character cells backwards within the row, map each code through $7700 and write the companion colour. Advance source, destination and colour by forty cells, stopping at the screen cutoff near $43E7.
Consume source bytes through $2A/$2B. Copy literals and use $06 to introduce a repeated character and count. Write the colour for each output cell from $7700. Stop at the selected destination limit.
Compare the output pointer with the section's limit at $03EC/$03ED. Continue decoding while the pointer is below the limit.
Use the divider at $2A04 to pace the countdown at $2A05. Request sound $88 at $0F and, at zero, redraw the preceding section if a transition is clear.
Sample the joystick. When there is no section transition, reset the idle counter and decrement the movement timer, falling through to the movement routine on expiry.
Reload the movement timer, move the player and sample the surface cell. Restart the scene when the sampled character is absent from the fifteen accepted codes at $29B6.

Toggle the walk pose index and choose a horizontal step. Test the four active-low direction bits in $28 and update position and orientation for each pressed direction. With no direction pressed, select a standing pose from the facing state when the idle counter is nonnegative.
Add $29A2 to sprite 0 low X and copy it to sprites 1–3. On carry, set the high X bits for all four. Preserve A.
Subtract $29A2 from sprite 0 low X and copy it to sprites 1–3. On borrow, clear the high X bits for all four. Preserve A.

Compute the screen row from sprite 2 Y and the column from sprite 0 X with a facing-dependent offset. Save the pointers to the corresponding cells and put the character from the first matrix in $29A3.
Give sprites 1–3 the same low X as sprite 0 and arrange the lower two pieces $15 pixels below the top pair. Set the standard player colours.
Set colours 2, 7, 2 and 7 for sprites 0 through 3.
Use sprite 0 Y as the upper coordinate for sprites 1 and 2 and move sprites 0 and 3 down $15 pixels. Change their colours for the fire pose.
Restore the ordinary vertical split using sprite 1 Y and reset the four player colours.
Choose the first or second quartet according to the transition count, then select the table and orientation from the facing state.
Restore the player sprite arrangement, request sound $89 and clear the score. Alternate two pose quartets for 40 timer delays, call $0ECD and restart the scene.
Fill the 1000 visible screen cells with character $0B and clear their colour RAM.

Prepare the VIC display mode, cycle the background colour for 32 timer delays, then call the movement routine ten times with synthetic up input. Restore the saved stack and return with the scene outcome byte decremented.
Advance this index when $2932 expires. Indices one through four select a pointer from $292C for the contacted hazard sprite. At five the handler instead disables the sprite and clears the index.
Five VIC frame pointers for the hit animation. The normal index update advances from zero to one before the first read at $28BC.
Decremented on the sprite contact path during the fire animation. The animation clears its sound request on completion when this counter is zero.
The raster path at $28A6 decrements the divider and reloads five when it advances the hazard hit frame.
The main loop uses this flag to select the retreat update. The timed update also tests it before requesting a section redraw.
The movement routine writes direction 0 through 3. The fire and retreat sprite updates use it to select poses and orientation.
Bit 2 toggles between two four-sprite poses for walking and for the failure animation.
Four shape pointers used by the idle path at $266B and $267E.
Four shape pointers used by the idle path at $2658 and $2691.
Two quartets of walking sprite pointers selected by the pose index at $29A1.
Two quartets of retreat pointers used by the branches at $27F2 and $2805.
Two quartets of retreat pointers used by the branches at $27DF and $2818.
Two quartets of sprite pointers alternated by the failure routine at $2858.
Ten little-endian pointers indexed by twice the section number. Sections 1–9 select packed screen characters at $4400–$4B50.
Ten little-endian indexed output addresses. The section routine also adds $9800 to the selected address for the colour output.
Ten little-endian screen limits used to stop the section decoder. After decoding, the renderer subtracts $4F from the selected limit to obtain the first source row for the downward copy.
The movement path decrements this byte for each pressed direction and tests its sign before selecting a standing pose.
The normal movement update decrements this divider and reloads it with two when it runs the position and surface checks.
Index of the end of the selected walk or restart quartet. The frame loop counts down from this index.
Low X increment or decrement for the two player-group movement routines.
The sampled character under the player group, compared against the list at $29B6.
Signed byte subtracted from sprite 0 Y for each transition step indexed by $29B1.
Animation step for the section transition. It selects when to redraw and when to clear the transition flag.
The retreat routine tests its sign before subtracting the additional section-specific vertical displacement.

Three zero slots between the signed retreat flag and the walkable-character list. The terrain comparison at $2531 starts its lookup at $29B6. The same slots precede the retained list in Phantom Knight.
The 15 character values accepted by the terrain test at $2531.
Six sprite 0 frame indices for the fire animation used by the branches at $2232 and $225C.
Six sprite 4 frame indices paired with the sprite 0 table at $29C5.
Interleaved signed X and Y offsets for the companion sprite in one fire animation. The orientation change negates the X entries.
Interleaved signed X and Y offsets used by the other fire animation. The orientation change negates the X entries.
Seven sprite 0 frame indices for the branches at $2208 and $2286.
Seven sprite 4 frame indices paired with the sprite 0 table at $29ED.
Saved orientation of the fire pose. At $2308 the routine compares against this byte to decide whether to negate the offsets.
Signed X and Y offsets for sprite 4 relative to sprite 0.
The main loop uses this flag to service the fire animation. The final frame clears it.
Animation counter advanced by $21CE and adapted into the zero-based pose index in X.
Four consecutive frame pointers assembled at $22DB and moved to the first four sprite slots in the order 0, 3, 2, 1.
Decremented at $24DF. Reloaded from $2A2C before advancing the section countdown at $2A05.
Timer loaded from the selected section preset. The update requests sound at $0F and checks for a section change at zero.
Ten timer values indexed by the section number at $2390. The chosen value is stored at $2A05 and decremented by the timed update at $24EB.
Index from two down to zero for sprite slots 7 through 5 during the collision update.
Controls when collision registers are sampled. Normally reloaded with two and set to seven on the sprite contact path.
Three indices changed by the background collision masks. Each selects one of the four diagonal movement cases.
Three sprite-animation indices advanced modulo four by the hazard update at $208C.
Four pointers used in the two movement cases with increasing X.
Four pointers used in the two movement cases with decreasing X.
Interleaved low X and Y for sprites 5 through 7, copied to the VIC register pairs beginning at $D00A.
Interleaved low X and Y for sprites 6 and 7 when the section selector is four.
Background and sprite collision latch bytes sampled from $D01F and $D01E and checked against the active sprite mask.
Divider reload value used by $24E5 after $2A04 reaches zero.
Zero slot between the section divider reload and the screen row-copy width. The timer read at $24E5 uses $2A2C and the renderer sets the width at $2A2E.
The section routine writes $27 here. The row copy starts at one less than this value and works down to offset zero.
Starts at ten and decrements after each of the final sequence's synthetic up moves.
Twice the selected VIC sprite number, used as the index for the sprite's Y coordinate at $203A.
Previous section index compared with $2962 so $1871 can run after a change.
Sprite slot index saved after installing the contact pointer $74 in the active fire path.
Cleared after the initial section drawing loop. The section renderer checks it before allowing the restart path.
The first byte is $EA. The bytes at $2A35 and $2A36 are the address operand of the Weapons Room store to $D004 that originally began one byte earlier.
Weapons Room projectile update from the branch testing low-X wrap. The following code updates the high X bit, vertical speed and horizontal acceleration.
Requests sound $8A and increments sprite 2 colour between timer updates, ending with colour $0D.
Select pose 8 and enter the shared Weapons Room retry delay.
Request sound $89, wait with A=$28, invoke resident failure handling and jump to the scene initialization address.
Use A to index sprite 2 frame and coordinate inputs, merge its high X mask, set colour zero and enable the sprite.
Use A as a countdown in $2EC9. Run the body between calls to the resident timer wait.
Use A as a countdown in $2EC6. On each pass wait on the resident timer, poll the joystick and update the sprite 1 animation.
Update the nested timers at $31A1 and $31A2. When they advance, select frame $BA plus the nested index for sprite 1.
Use A times 90 to locate the selected resident pose record at $3200 and copy it to zero page beginning at $44.
Multiply A by eighteen and add $304C. Load positions, colours and frame pointers for sprites 4–7. Replace the upper nibbles of the VIC expansion masks with the final two fields.
Retained Weapons Room routine. Use A to select sprite 0 coordinates, expansion bits and a source pointer. Select frame $A9 and build it at $6A40 from an initial zero count and source literals.

Retained Weapons Room routine. Reset the band index and select the bank and character matrix. Schedule $2C58 at the line in $99 and apply the first group of coordinates, colours and frame pointers to sprites 5–7.
Retained Weapons Room routine. Set the next interrupt to $2C98 at the line in $9A. Use the second group of coordinates, colours and frame pointers for sprites 5–7.
Retained Weapons Room routine. Set the next interrupt to $2CD8 at the line in $9B. Use the third group of coordinates, colours and frame pointers for sprites 5–7.
Retained Weapons Room routine. Set the next interrupt to $2D18 at the line in $9C. Use the fourth group of coordinates, colours and frame pointers for sprites 5–7.
Retained Weapons Room routine. Set the next interrupt to $2D58 at the line in $9D. Use the fifth group of coordinates, colours and frame pointers for sprites 5–7.
Retained Weapons Room routine. Set the next interrupt to $2C07 at raster line 1. Use the sixth group of coordinates, colours and frame pointers for sprites 5–7.
Retained Weapons Room routine. Service the resident sound and tape port at $1783 and jump to the shared IRQ return.
Retained Weapons Room routine. Advance the band index, schedule $2C07 at raster line 1 and select VIC bank $0000 with $D018=$15 before returning through the IRQ epilogue.
Retained Weapons Room routine. When the index at $316D reaches six, clear it and the active flag, then store character 1 at the saved cell pointer and colour $0C at its companion colour address.

Retained Weapons Room routine. Decrement the divider at $316C. At zero advance the index at $316D and reload the divider to seven. Use the index loaded before the increment to select a character from $317F, then set its cell colour to 1.
Retained Weapons Room routine. Use A times two to select the screen cell pointer from $316F, then initialize the character index to zero and divider to one. Decrement the activity byte at $316E.
Retained Weapons Room routine. Wait through the shared raster synchronization and put the six-band handler entry $2C07 in $42/$43.
Retained Weapons Room routine. Use source $7400 and destination $4000, then fall through to the matrix copy and colour update.
Retained Weapons Room routine. Use source $4000 and destination $0400. Share the copy loop, which skips the eight sprite pointer positions before applying the colour lookup in page $46.
Retained Weapons Room routine. Use A as a movement count. Increase the three low X coordinates in each of the six pose bands and move sprite 0 right, setting its high X on wrap.
Retained Weapons Room routine. Use A as a movement count. Decrease the three low X coordinates in each of the six pose bands and the low X of sprite 0.
Retained Weapons Room routine. Pass three consecutive sprite indices $CB through $CD to the shared sprite transform at $16AD.
An authored zero slot between the mirror routine return and the weapon sequence countdown.
Retained Weapons Room data. Countdown set before the Weapons Room movement and input sequences. The timed update at $2B03 also uses it.
Retained Weapons Room data. Set to 16 at $2A92 and decremented between sprite 2 colour increments.
Zero slot between the flash countdown at $2EC7 and the wait countdown at $2EC9.
Retained Weapons Room data. Iteration counter used by the sprite follow loop and the timed wait at $2AF2.
Two zero bytes before the six packed shape pointers at $2ECC. The shape pointer index uses $2ECC as its base.
Retained Weapons Room data. Nineteen little-endian pointers selected by twice the shape index in the sprite 0 builder at $2BDF.
Retained Weapons Room data. Nineteen pairs of low X and Y coordinates loaded into sprite 0 by the shape builder.
Retained Weapons Room data. One sprite 0 horizontal expansion bit per shape index, merged into $D01D.
Retained Weapons Room data. One sprite 0 vertical expansion bit per shape index, merged into $D017.
Retained Weapons Room data. Packed sprite 0 frame. The first byte requests 35 zero bytes. The following 29 source bytes, through $2F5B, complete the frame at $6A40.
Retained Weapons Room data. Packed sprite 0 frame. The first byte requests 39 zero bytes. The following 25 source bytes, through $2F74, complete the frame at $6A40.

Retained Weapons Room data. Packed sprite 0 frame. The first byte requests 15 zero bytes. The following 49 source bytes, through $3024, complete the frame at $6A40.
Retained Weapons Room data. Packed sprite 0 frame. The first byte requests 24 zero bytes. The following 40 source bytes, through $304C, complete the frame at $6A40.
Sixteen 18-byte records selected by the loader at $2B56. Each holds eight position bytes, four sprite colours, four frame pointers and the two expansion masks for sprites 4–7.
Retained Weapons Room data. Divider, current character index and activity flag for the cell animation at $2DBB–$2E18.
Retained Weapons Room data. Eight screen cell address pairs available to the selector at $2DFF.
Retained Weapons Room data. Five consecutive character codes indexed by the cell animation at $2DEA.
Retained Weapons Room data. Reset in the first raster handler and incremented by subsequent handlers.
Retained Weapons Room data. Seven frame pointers available to the sprite 2 preset selector.
Retained Weapons Room data. Seven pairs of low X and Y coordinates available to the sprite 2 preset selector.
Retained Weapons Room data. Seven high X masks merged into bit 2 of $D010 when a projectile preset is selected.
Retained Weapons Room data. Two counters decremented and reloaded by $2B15.

Retained Weapons Room data. Projectile initialization record. The update at $2A21 reads the divider reload, divider, X and Y velocities, X and Y adjustments and the threshold at $31A9. The scene also writes $31AA with its presets.

Retained Weapons Room data. Seven six-character rows for the Weapons Room sequence at $26DE. The first row copies columns 0–4. The next six copy columns 0–5. Destination rows start at $41CF with zero written to the corresponding colour cells.
This scene record ends with the eleven byte marker copied by the unpacker at $0DDE.
The first page of the screen matrix for the background in VIC bank $4000. Its character codes index the scene colour lookup when the display is initialized.
